outcome: An accelerated-compute platform where storage and network fabric are sized to keep the accelerators fully fed.
overview: Research institutions buying accelerated compute usually discover that the interesting constraints are not the accelerators: power draw per rack, cooling capacity, the storage bandwidth needed to keep the accelerators busy, and the network fabric between nodes. The Dell AI Factory design with NVIDIA covers that whole stack as an engineered configuration. The sizing conversation should start at the facility and at the workload profile, because an accelerator estate the building cannot power is the most expensive kind of mistake available here.

benefits.text: Accelerators, storage, fabric and facility requirements are engineered together rather than assembled
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

benefits.text: Storage bandwidth is sized to keep the accelerators busy rather than to hold the data
benefits.limits: Bandwidth sizing depends on the workload profile; a design sized for training behaves differently under an inference-heavy load

benefits.text: Research data and model weights stay inside the institution’s own facility
benefits.limits: Residency is a property of the deployment; it says nothing about licensing of the datasets or the models used on it

residency: All compute, data and model weights remain inside the institution’s own facility

notFor.situation: An institution able to use cloud accelerator capacity for its workloads
notFor.why: On-premises accelerated compute carries facility and lifecycle costs that rented capacity does not

notFor.situation: A workload set with no measured accelerator demand
notFor.why: Sizing without measured demand produces a facility commitment against an assumption

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with accredited Dell and NVIDIA implementation partners · Duration: 16–24 weeks to a first workload in production, dominated by accelerator lead time
Support model: Vendor hardware support across compute, storage and fabric; Redington coordinates the vendor cases across all three.
1) Profile and verify — workload demand profiled, facility power, cooling and rack verified
2) Design — accelerator, storage and fabric sizing, allocation model
3) Build — nodes, storage and fabric installed and validated under load
4) Onboard and hand over — first research workload in production, capacity planning handed over
deliverables: Measured accelerator utilisation under a representative workload meets the design figure
Storage delivers the bandwidth the design assumed, verified under load
Facility draw under full load is within the verified capacity
effort: 16–24 weeks to a first workload in production, dominated by accelerator lead time
languages: English delivery; Arabic executive materials on request
